<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via registerAction (symbol, a method of class ActionsFacet))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 135c2fb82fcd2aeee208b6a8a372209c80655489` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3bab68ea9259cb0a4ba90b67313ff27286e2d8f0` — the merge of head `accb6240985b185dd97422ccb4504f535631aded` into base `135c2fb82fcd2aeee208b6a8a372209c80655489`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3bab68ea9259cb0a4ba90b67313ff27286e2d8f0 && git checkout 3bab68ea9259cb0a4ba90b67313ff27286e2d8f0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 135c2fb82fcd2aeee208b6a8a372209c80655489 accb6240985b185dd97422ccb4504f535631aded && git checkout -B drift-repro 135c2fb82fcd2aeee208b6a8a372209c80655489 && git merge --no-ff accb6240985b185dd97422ccb4504f535631aded

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 135c2fb82fcd2aeee208b6a8a372209c80655489
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 135c2fb82fcd2aeee208b6a8a372209c80655489` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `76e59ff173db77342e707ce7607ac5a2ec3a45af`
Local-runs: probe — in a throwaway worktree at the head (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `OS_SKIP_DTS=1 turbo run build` over the objectql, cloud-connection, cli and metadata-protocol closures, 63 tasks): the PR's pins `vitest run src/plugin-authored-actions.test.ts src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts` in objectql (38/38), `src/marketplace-install-local-override-gate.test.ts` in cloud-connection (12/12), `src/utils/override-declarations.test.ts` in cli (11/11), `src/protocol.packaged-base-refusal.test.ts` in metadata-protocol (91/91); full `pnpm test` of cloud-connection, objectql and metadata-protocol (cloud-connection 70 files, 880/880; objectql 552 files, 11027/11027; metadata-protocol 317 files passed, 4 skipped, 22450 passed / 26 skipped; each exit 0); `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` exit 0 (its level axis reports NOT APPLICABLE with no PR payload, so it graded no declaration locally) and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` exit 0; one reviewer probe, a throwaway cli test calling `findOverrideDeclarationRefusals` (the `os validate` walk) on a declared action override whose `objectName` is another object's, run twice (see ①.6); one ablation, `git restore --source=origin/main` of `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` (the whole of fix 2 removed), metadata-protocol rebuilt with the fix's marker `overrideWriteActionObjectOf` counted 0 in `dist/*.js`: `protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts` 1 failed / 13 passed, exactly the moved-object pin (`expected undefined to match object { code, status }`, the save admitted it); restore leg `git checkout HEAD -- path`, rebuilt, marker 3 in `dist/index.js`, 14/14, probe file deleted, `git status --porcelain` empty; worktree removed afterwards.
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-actions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-override-gate.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin-authored-actions.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-artifact-lookup.ts (`shippedArtifactsOf`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`SchemaRegistry#getArtifactItem`, the prefer-local and composite-scan tiers), packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts (`standaloneActionOwnerKey`), packages/cli/src/utils/override-declarations.ts (`findOverrideDeclarationRefusals`, the `os validate` walk) and its test on `origin/main`, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts (the `registerAction` binder, `owner`), packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts (`resolveRouteActionDeclaration`, the ADR-0066 D4 gate), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts `rehydrate` and `handleInstall` (register before `bindArtifactHandlers`), docs/adr/0146 D9, .changeset/30542-action-override-doors-and-boot-order.md (prose face, read for its declaration lines, levels and marker), content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx and skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md (read for the Skills-docs line)

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line-initial on the PR body and the changeset). `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` on the nine changed paths decides no schema or governed face and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries the `(narrowing)` arm, so `--face narrowing` sets the tier; the Scope floor is every path of the diff outside the prose face. Review by an isolated reader of PR #30612 (card #30542, which names four items from the contract reviews of PR #30497 / #30065). Reads: the card body, the PR body, the dev report (comment 6665387535, read for its claims only), `git diff 739c9727...76e59ff1` (9 files, +222 −28; the head is the fix merged with `origin/main` at `739c9727`; `origin/main` has since moved to `55d9dd44`), the files in Scope at this head and on `origin/main` where named, the head's check-runs via REST (two readings, see ③). No reading below is taken from the dev's self-report; where the report's number appears it is beside my own.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Fix 1, the install-door ratchet** (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, `evaluateOverrideWriteGate`). The gate's `shippers` are still read off the protocol's per-package listing keyed by `listedIdentity` (`OBJECT:NAME` for an action), unchanged. What moves is the item handed to `judgeOverrideWrite` as `baseItemOf(base)`: for an installed (not delivered) base it is now `registry.getArtifactItem(type, name, base)` kept only when it is a plain object stamped `_packageId === base` whose `listedIdentity` equals the incoming item's identity (so the same object), else the listed item as before. `SchemaRegistry#getArtifactItem` with a `currentPackageId` resolves prefer-local (`base:name`) and returns only a code artifact, so the judge now sees the base's own action, not the armed override the listing serves under the base's envelope. A delivered base is still read off its body; a registry without `getArtifactItem` (the older harness cases) answers as before. This widens the install door's accept set to the save door's (`overrideWriteVerdict` already judged against the shipping artifact): the card's pin, a v2 back at the base's gates, is admitted, and the CONTROL (v2 dropping `ai.requiresConfirmation`) stays refused `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / `declared_action_widens_access` with nothing saved. The pin runs the real install route (`plugin.start` registers it on the raw app, the case posts to it). **Right and complete against item 1.**
2. **Fix 2, `objectName` pinned at the protocol door** (`protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`). A private `overrideWriteActionObjectOf` reads `item.objectName` (string, else `''`), and `overrideWriteItemsOf` is refactored onto it with identical semantics (I compared the two expressions: a non-empty string `objectName` gives `OBJECT:NAME`, anything else the bare name). `overrideWriteVerdict` gains `onItsObject`, applied to the `shippers` set and to `baseItemOf` only when the request carries a declaration and the type folds to `action`: a shipping artifact on another object is no shipper, so the declared moved-object override is refused `declared_package_ships_no_such_item`, the rule `os validate` and the install door give it. An undeclared item, and every non-action type, is judged exactly as before (the `onItsObject` short-circuits are the first two disjuncts). `judgeOverrideWrite` itself is untouched. The pin goes through the real `protocol.saveMetaItem` on a real engine and asserts `code: NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, `status: 403` (ADR-0112 envelope), the rule, no stored row, every read still serving `SHIPPED`, and a CONTROL on the base's own object admitted. The dev's choice not to add an `action` row to `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` is right: that table keys `SchemaRegistry` bundle collections and the protocol list merge, so a row would re-key every action read. **Right and complete against item 2.**
3. **Fix 3, only the declared base slots beneath** (`engine-actions.ts`, `engine.ts`, `plugin.ts`). `registerActionOverride` gains an optional fifth argument `base`, recorded on the entry; the resync (`plugin.ts` 4208, the only caller in `packages/*/src`) passes `action.overrides?.package`. `registerAction` under a key an override holds slots beneath only when `arrivesAsDeclaredBase` holds: the arriving registration names a package, and either the override recorded no `base` (legacy behaviour kept) or `registry.getArtifactItem('action', actionName)` is stamped `_packageId === override.base` with `standaloneActionOwnerKey(artifact) === objectName`. That is the same lookup `isDeclaredArtifactActionOverride` binds the override by once the artifact is registered (both pass no package to `getArtifactItem`), so the run and the resync judge by one predicate; in the two-shipper misconfiguration both decline the row, consistently. The ordering premise holds on every path I read: `AppPlugin.start` binds through `bindAppArtifactHandlers` after `registerApp`; the install (`handleInstall` step 4c) and the `kernel:ready` rehydrate both call `bindArtifactHandlers` after `manifestService.register`. `ActionsHost` gains `registry` through the `actionsHost` getter in `engine.ts`; the read is optional-chained, so a test double without a registry still works. The pin (real `ObjectQL`, real `ObjectQLPlugin` resync, a spied `getArtifactItem`) shows the other-base row running until the real base binds, then `ran:BASE BODY`, one collision warning naming both owners, `isServedOverrideRowOf(row, BASE) === false` and `(row, OTHER) === true`, and the next resync leaving the base bound. **Right and complete against item 3**; the dev's reason for not choosing the `metadata:reloaded` broadcast (it re-runs every consumer's `kernel:ready` sweep from inside the install plugin's own `kernel:ready`) is sound, and the card offered either tightening.
4. **Fix 3 does not widen who may run an action.** Who may run is decided at the route by `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` (`runtime/src/domains/actions.ts`, ADR-0066 D4) from the served declaration (the registry artifact or the authored row), never from the handler entry; the handler stack decides only which body runs. The new replace-and-warn branch is the pre-existing collision branch that `registerAction` already took on `main` for any two packages without an override in play. What changes is one case: another package's handler no longer slots beneath an override it is not the declared base of, so the body that runs for the key becomes the arriving package's instead of the override's, with the same warning any collision prints. No gate is dropped; the gates come from the declaration the reads serve, which already declined that row. **No widening.**
5. **Fix 4, log level.** `packageName === undefined` returns `false` from `arrivesAsDeclaredBase`, so an unpackaged registration under an armed override replaces it through the warning branch (`replacedPackage: 'metadata-service'`, `package: undefined`) — the behaviour the `registerAction` docblock promised; the docblock in `engine.ts` is re-spelled to name the declared base's handler as the one exception. The card asked warn or docblock and the dev did warn, with the pin asserting one warning and the unpackaged body running. **Right.**
6. **`os validate` on `main` already refused the moved-object declared override** — my own reading, not the dev's table. A throwaway cli test calling `findOverrideDeclarationRefusals` with a base shipping `log_call` on `crm_account` and its `.custom` pair declaring `overrides` on `log_call` with `objectName: 'partner_lead'`: refused `[PAIR, 'declared_package_ships_no_such_item']`; CONTROL on `crm_account` admitted. Run against the head's build (2/2) and again with `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` restored from `origin/main` and metadata-protocol rebuilt, fix 2 absent from `dist` (2/2, same two verdicts). The cli walk keys an action `OBJECT:NAME` through `overrideWriteItemsOf` on `main` already (`origin/main:packages/cli/src/utils/override-declarations.ts` lines 109–128, and its committed control at line 65, "an action on another object"), and the install door keys the same way through `listedIdentity`. So two of the three doors, the CLI included, refused this shape before this PR; the save door alone admitted it. Ruling in ③.
7. **Public surface.** `@objectstack/objectql`: `ObjectQL#registerActionOverride` gains an optional trailing parameter and `ActionHandlerEntry` an optional `base` — a widening of a public signature, nothing removed or retyped. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: one private helper, no export change. `@objectstack/cloud-connection`: a private type widened. All three packages publish (`private` unset), so a changeset on each is owed and present. `packages/spec` untouched, no generated artifact owed.
8. **Card closure.** `Fixes #30542` is right: items 1–3 fixed with the three pins the card asked for, item 4 answered with a named choice, one ablation per fix recorded by the dev and one reproduced here. First body line references the card; target `main`; draft; head repo = base repo; author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
9. **Acceptance note read.** The dev's note that the pair's undeclared same-named action on another object is still refused `undeclared_same_name` at the protocol door while `os validate` and the install door admit it is a true, pre-existing disagreement in the stricter direction, outside this card and not widened here; a card for it is the lane seat's, not this PR's.

### ② Semver level

**Inconsistent with the ruling — must-fix M1.** The dev declares `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and grades `minor` on all three packages. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 the line is "the change to what a metadata author can write", and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` ruling A grades the level from that line alone (`none` takes `patch`; "`none` beside a `minor` is the half of the ruling with teeth"). What an author can write is the verdict table `os validate` gives, and ①.6 measures that `os validate` refused this exact shape on `main`: the protocol did not narrow, one door caught up to the verdict the other two already gave (Prime Directive #10, declared vs enforced). That is the precedent of record 6663292380 on PR #30564 (#30095), where the object publish door caught up to a CLI verdict and the line was ruled `none` with `patch`; the counter-precedent (PR #30270, `narrowed`) was the case where the CLI verdict itself moved. Nothing in `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` moves, no key or value an author writes is added or refused by the rule table. The right declaration is `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, on the PR body and in the changeset. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` stays right (`yes`: the install door's accept set and a public signature widen; the arm: the save door's accept set narrows), the `!` title, the BREAKING banner and the one ADR-0087 marker stay — "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". Both local changeset gates exit 0 on the head as declared; they would exit 0 on the corrected declaration too (the gate's two contradictions are `added` under `no` and `narrowed` without an arm). The ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right at this head: no schema key moves, nothing at rest is rewritten, and a moved-object override never ran there (its handler was never rebound), so there is no FROM to TO to prescribe.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Metadata-protocol `narrowed` vs `none`: `none`**, with the reasoning and the measurement in ①.6 and ②. The dev's argument ("a declared override shape the save door accepted is now refused") describes an accept-set narrowing at one door, which the `(narrowing)` arm already carries; it is not a change to the protocol's own verdict. Must-fix M1.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up #30505`.** No sentence in `skills/**` or `content/docs/**` becomes false with this PR. `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` line 128 lists the overridable types without `action` and says nothing about an action's object; `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` line 52 shows the `overrides` shape only. `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx` lines 132–134 say an `action` override "waits for ADR-0146 D9's conditions and is not served yet": that sentence is false on `main` already, made false by PR #30497 (`bcdf8d34`), not by this PR, and the doc was last touched by #30380 — it belongs to the #30505 docs card, which today names only the skill file. No doc states that an action override may change the action's object, so nothing here turns false; `follow-up #30505` is the right spelling and no edit is owed in this PR. The sentence the seat should add to #30505 is in the hand-back and repeated here: "A declared action override keeps the base action's `objectName`: every door (the save and publish doors, `os validate`, the managed install) matches the base's action by `OBJECT:NAME`, and an override that moves the action to another object is refused `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` with rule `declared_package_ships_no_such_item`; and `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx` lines 132–134 still say an `action` override is not served yet, false since PR #30497 — correct it in the same docs change." Should-fix S2 for that card, not this PR.
- **Should-fix S1 (not blocking; pre-existing text, same at all three doors):** the refusal `declared_package_ships_no_such_item` reads "ships no action named 'X'" and offers "correct the name", which for the moved-object case names neither the object nor the fix (keep the base's `objectName`); the changeset body carries that remedy but the runtime message does not. The message is `judgeOverrideWrite`'s on `main` and `os validate` prints the same, so it is a prescription-quality card for the lane, not a change this PR must make.
- **Observation, no action:** `overrideWriteActionObjectOf`, `listedIdentity` and the old `overrideWriteItemsOf` read `objectName` only, while the runtime key `standaloneActionOwnerKey` also reads `object`; the three doors agree with each other, and the spec's `ActionSchema` declares `objectName`, so no door disagrees on an authorable shape. Pre-existing and outside this card.
- **Pins go through the real doors with CONTROLs** — ①.1 (install route, 200 saved vs 403 nothing written), ①.2 (`protocol.saveMetaItem`, `overrideWriteVerdict` refuse vs admit), ①.3 (resync and run on a real engine, `isServedOverrideRowOf` both ways). Ablation reproduced here with its own numbers (Local-runs); the dev's four ablations are recorded in the PR body and the report.
- **Dogfood battery.** The `Dogfood Regression Gate (n/3)` shards are skipped on `pull_request` and the aggregate check is `success` with shards `skipped`, so CI carries no dogfood reading for this PR; the dev's reading names this head (`76e59ff17`, 420 files passed / 3 skipped, 3496 tests passed / 36 skipped, VERDICT exit 0 under the verify lock), full, no red. NOT MEASURED locally; the `!` / `(narrowing)` entry requirement is met on the dev's pinned reading. The diff moves no send or write after an answer.
- **Check-runs on `76e59ff17`** (REST, three readings, last at 2026-11-05T18:25Z): 33 `success`, 13 `skipped` (opt-in and non-PR jobs), 1 `in_progress` (`Test Core (4/8)`), **0 failures**. `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1–3 and 5–8, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` are all `success`. `Check Changeset` passed on the head as declared and reads the declaration lines as carriers, so it does not decide ②; after M1 it passes on `none` + `patch` by the gate's own text. Not governed (`check-governed-merges` exit 0 per the dispatch); enqueue waits on M1 and on the last shard.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay) — no external login to name. `security_findings: none`, `open_questions: []`, `premise_still_valid: true`; nothing security-shaped beyond the PR's own stated rule was seen.

### ④ Design judgment (narrowing face)

Judged against the published spec on `main`: does the narrowing take a declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real? **It makes the spec's refusal real.** ADR-0146 D2 and D9 admit a declared override only of an item the base ships, and the one identity every door names an action by is `OBJECT:NAME` (`overrideWriteItemsOf`, the walk `os validate` and the install door already took on `main`); the save door matched by name alone, so it admitted a declaration the protocol's own rule refused, and the admitted row never ran anywhere (its handler was keyed on the other object and never rebound). No author loses an override that worked. The three doors now give one answer from one helper, and the narrowing is scoped by two guards (a declaration present, type `action`) so nothing else moves. Fix 1 is the mirror in the widening direction: the install door judged against the listing's envelope, which after arming is the override itself, so a ratchet the protocol never declared is removed and the install door judges against the same artifact the save door does. Fix 3 closes the one case where the run and the reads disagreed, by the predicate the reads already use, and keeps the legacy behaviour for an override bound without a base, so no caller of the public method is broken. The cited code is read, not reviewed. **Holds**, with the level and line corrected per M1.

Must-fix: M1 (②). Should-fix: S1, S2 (③), both cards for the lane seat, not changes to this PR. Observations: ③ object-key spelling.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-izhot2`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CbPxYq1wQmUNWvMZkC`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Must-fixes:
- M1 — `Metadata-protocol: none` (not `narrowed`) on the PR body and the changeset, and `patch` (not `minor`) on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/cloud-connection` in `.changeset/30542-action-override-doors-and-boot-order.md`; keep `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, the `!`, the BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 marker and the `Skills-docs: follow-up #30505` line. Measured in ①.6; ruling in ②. A declaration-only head: the same reviewer's delta review suffices.

## Contract review (delta)

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `accb6240985b185dd97422ccb4504f535631aded`
